title: Efficient Quantum Simulation of Linearized Vlasov--Poisson Dynamics Using Trotter and THRIFT Hamiltonian Simulation Methods
authors: Kartick Paul, Rahul V, S. Aravinda, Reetesh K. Gangwar
abstract: The Vlasov--Poisson system provides the fundamental kinetic description of plasma and plays a central role in understanding collective phenomena such as Landau damping and wave--particle interactions. Efficient numerical simulation of these dynamics remains challenging because of the high dimensionality of phase space. In this work, we studied magnetized and non-magnetized plasma using a quantum simulation framework for the linearized Vlasov-Poisson equation by reformulating the discretized system as a Hermitian Hamiltonian suitable for gate-based quantum computation. The time evolution is implemented using first, second and fourth-order Trotter--Suzuki product formulas and the recently proposed Time-Resolved Interaction Framework (THRIFT). The performance of the different simulation methods is systematically evaluated through electric field evolution, state fidelity, convergence behavior, energy conservation, entanglement entropy and quantum resource requirements, including circuit depth and two-qubit gate complexity, for both magnetized and non-magnetized plasma models. To further reduce finite time step errors without increasing circuit depth, Richardson extrapolation is incorporated as a error-mitigation technique. The results provide a comprehensive comparison of Trotter and THRIFT approaches and establish practical guidelines for accurate and resource-efficient quantum simulation of plasma dynamics on gate-based quantum computers.
summary: This paper tackles the difficult quantum simulation of plasma dynamics governed by the Vlasov-Poisson system by mapping it onto a quantum Hamiltonian. It systematically compares the performance of Trotter-Suzuki and THRIFT time-evolution methods. The results establish that advanced techniques, particularly THRIFT combined with Richardson extrapolation, provide a resource-efficient pathway for accurate quantum simulation of plasma physics.
main_problem: The core challenge is developing efficient quantum simulation protocols for the high-dimensional, non-equilibrium dynamics described by the linearized Vlasov-Poisson system.
main_result: The study provides a comprehensive comparison showing that the THRIFT framework, combined with higher-order Trotter formulas and Richardson extrapolation, offers a resource-efficient path to accurately simulating plasma dynamics on gate-based quantum computers.
method: The time evolution operator $e^{-iHt}$ is approximated using product formulas (Trotter-Suzuki and THRIFT) and the resulting errors are systematically reduced using Richardson extrapolation.
model_or_system: The system is the linearized Vlasov-Poisson equation describing plasma dynamics, which is reformulated into a Hermitian Hamiltonian $H = H_{	ext{stream}} + H_{	ext{electric}} + H_{	ext{magnetic}}$ suitable for quantum simulation.
key_observables: Electric field evolution, state fidelity, energy conservation, entanglement entropy, and quantum resource requirements (circuit depth, two-qubit gate complexity).
important_parameters: The small parameter $\alpha$ (related to the Hamiltonian decomposition $H = H_0 + \alpha H_1$) and the time step $\Delta t$ are crucial for error analysis.
main_assumptions: The plasma is linearized, considering only electron dynamics with ions treated as a fixed background, and the simulation is mapped onto a gate-based quantum computation model.
figures_summary: Figures compare probability distributions and extracted electric-field energy between exact evolution and various simulation orders (e.g., 1st-order Trotter vs. THRIFT), demonstrating the error suppression achieved by higher-order methods and Richardson extrapolation.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the physical model and Hamiltonian, details the quantum simulation techniques (Trotter vs. THRIFT), systematically evaluates performance across multiple diagnostics (fidelity, energy, resources), and concludes by establishing practical guidelines for resource-efficient simulation.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the computational bottleneck of simulating complex many-body physics (like plasma) on near-term quantum hardware by rigorously comparing advanced quantum simulation algorithms.

Figure 1 shows the electric-field energy obtained from the exact Hamiltonian evolution together with the corre- sponding Trotter–Suzuki and THRIFT approximations.

FIG. 2. Semi-logarithmic evolution of the normalized electric-field energy, E(t) = |Ex(t)|2 + |Ey(t)|2, for the mag- netized linearized Vlasov–Poisson system with kx = ky = 0.4 and B0 = 0.3. A 31 × 31 velocity-space discretization is used, giving312 + 2 = 963 physical degrees of freedom and a 1024- dimensional padded Hilbert space encoded by ten qubits. The black solid curve denotes the exact Hamiltonian evo- lution, while the colored curves show the first- and second- order Trotter–Suzuki (Tr.) and THRIFT (TH.) simulations for r = 20 and r = 40 decomposition steps.
